### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**7** anchor(s) derived from **2** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them. ⚠️ **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/ui.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/view.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/ui.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/view.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **58** of **210** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **168** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c48cd2c103a9dfa99313a67a3ec622291d793900` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `801961354ea0bbb9a31225002eae1829c3a7e9f5` — the merge of head `ea4b11b5e0b294a4d7adbc3ce2644a94a99a80c2` into base `c48cd2c103a9dfa99313a67a3ec622291d793900`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 801961354ea0bbb9a31225002eae1829c3a7e9f5 && git checkout 801961354ea0bbb9a31225002eae1829c3a7e9f5
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin c48cd2c103a9dfa99313a67a3ec622291d793900 ea4b11b5e0b294a4d7adbc3ce2644a94a99a80c2 && git checkout -B drift-repro c48cd2c103a9dfa99313a67a3ec622291d793900 && git merge --no-ff ea4b11b5e0b294a4d7adbc3ce2644a94a99a80c2

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c48cd2c103a9dfa99313a67a3ec622291d793900
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `ea4b11b5e0b294a4d7adbc3ce2644a94a99a80c2`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts + packages/lint/src/validate-list-view-field-refs.ts (the gate that judges the new key against the object, read as one change with it), packages/spec/liveness/view.json (the row that grades it), and the cited code read on the head: packages/spec/src/shared/identifiers.zod.ts (`SystemIdentifierSchema` L102-108), packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts (`SelectOptionSchema.value` L363-376, `picklist` L1558 and the one-source rule L2613-2641), ui/packages/plugin-kanban/src/ObjectKanban.tsx (`effectiveColumns` L1453-1482, the `Uncategorized` bucket L1819-1873), packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.ts L3533-3565, packages/lint/src/index.ts L549-560.

Inputs: card #28018 body and its three comments (claim 6526161926, file-surface amendment 6526184775 with the seat's option A, os-dev-report 6527607823); PR #28196 body, 12-file list and the diff against `main` (+457/-11); the check-runs on `ea4b11b5` (read 2026-10-30T16:54Z): 50 names, all `completed`, 39 `success`, 11 `skipped`, 0 `failure`; among the successes Governed Surface Queue Guard, Check Changeset, PR-body guards, Spec property liveness, Lint & Repo Gates, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · docs & code guards, Lint · repo & tooling gates, the three scoped lints, Type Check · workspace/source/consumer/debt ledger, Test Core 1/8-8/8, Test UI, Live E2E UI, Build Core, Build Docs, Build UI Deps, Dogfood Regression Gate. Author `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`, so no login note is owed. The reviewer is not the drafter (`session_01L9qibxL3MYcTjfshb8eeK3`).

### ① Derived judgments

1. `KanbanConfigSchema` (`view.zod.ts` L2061, a `strictObject`) gains one optional key `lanes: z.array(SystemIdentifierSchema).min(1)`, no default. The accept set widens on every surface that embeds the kanban block (the six tables in the regenerated `view.mdx`: list view config, view items, tabs) by exactly this key. Refused at parse: an empty list (`too_small`, with a message that says to omit the key), and an entry outside the `SystemIdentifierSchema` grammar (`invalid_format` at its own index). **Right**, and the grammar is the stored option value's own: `SelectOptionSchema.value` IS `SystemIdentifierSchema` (`field.zod.ts` L376), so a label such as `In Progress` is refused where a stored value is accepted, with no value a select option can carry being refused. Pinned by `kanban-config-lanes.test.ts` (member on the bare block and inside a list view with an unknown-key control, order kept, absence writes nothing, empty refused, label refused at its index).
2. Both refinements (`minItems`, the string pattern) project into the published JSON Schema, so `dropped-refinements.baseline.json` gains no row; the uniqueness check deliberately lives in lint for that reason. **Right** (`check:strictness-ledger` and `check:generated` are among the green gates).
3. Lint `validateListViewFieldRefs` (`validate-list-view-field-refs.ts` L1056-1140, L1283, L1373): `list-view-kanban-lane-repeated` (error, at the second entry) runs before the universe skip, needs no field map; `list-view-kanban-lane-unknown` (error, at `kanban.lanes[i]`, with `suggestName` against the field's inline option values) runs once the view's bound object resolved, i.e. after the existing `groupByField` judgment, and only when that field has a non-empty inline `options` array. A `picklist`-bound field has no inline options (`field.zod.ts` L2613-2641: one source, `options` or `picklist`), a boolean or lookup has none, so neither is judged; an unresolvable `groupByField` is `list-view-field-unknown` at that key and its lanes are not judged. **Right.** Both ids are exported from the barrel (L549-560) and explained in `os explain` (L3533-3565, every verdict and fix one line), as `rule-explanations.test.ts` requires. Pinned by `validate-list-view-kanban-lanes.test.ts` (11 cases incl. `validate`/`build` failing and the runtime save door reporting both ids).
4. Liveness (`liveness/view.json` L104): the `kanban` row keeps `live` and its note names `lanes` at PLANNED strength ahead of its reader, the `viewMode`-on-gantt precedent (L112), with the measured read (`ObjectKanban.tsx#effectiveColumns` draws one lane per declared option and reads no lane list). `Spec property liveness` is `success`. **Right**, and consistent with the file's own convention for a key riding a blanket row; no `authorWarn` is possible on a blanket row, so authors get the `planned` word from the describe and the changeset instead (see S1).
5. Generated surfaces: `authorable-surface/ui.json` adds `ui/KanbanConfig:lanes`; `view.mdx` carries the row in every kanban table; `protocol.mdx` and `object.mdx` are the regenerated spillover of the shared block. **Right.**

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/28018-kanban-lanes.md`: `@objectstack/spec` **minor** (one optional key, nothing removed or tightened: a board without `lanes` parses byte-identically), `@objectstack/lint` **minor** (two new error ids, reachable only when the key is authored). Both match what the diff publishes. `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: added` sit line-initial on the PR body and the changeset. **Consistent.**

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: none declared.
- The lint half (`validate-list-view-field-refs.ts`, its explanations, tests, `@objectstack/lint` changeset) is outside the order's first file surface and inside the seat's amendment 6526184775 (option A): the spec cannot see the object, so the membership refusal can only live where `groupByField` is judged. Answered in ①.3.
- `Skills-docs: follow-up owed` (`skills/objectstack-ui/rules/list-views.md` beside `groupByField`/`summarizeField`) and the `domain:ui` renderer half (`effectiveColumns` reads `lanes`): the seat's follow-up cards, as the PR body names them; the planned note is what makes the contract half sound alone.
- Alternative `hideEmptyLanes` not taken: the card offered both; the reasons (an empty lane stops being a drop target, lanes flicker as records move, no ordering) are stated on the schema docblock and hold.
- Serial constraint: #28138 (`calendar.initialDate`) edits `view.zod.ts` in the calendar region (claim 6526161926); no hunk overlap, ordinary concurrency.
- Author: `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no login note.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts` against the card (#28018: a lane key on the kanban config, an ordered list or a boolean; the console half to follow) and its first consumer:

- **The key holds against its consumer.** `effectiveColumns` (`ObjectKanban.tsx` L1453-1482) builds lanes either from explicit `columns: [{ id, title }]` or from the group field's options, with `id` = the option's stored value, and the `Uncategorized` lane (L1819-1873) is the display bucket for a card whose value matches no lane. `lanes` as an ordered list of stored values maps one-to-one onto those lane ids, so the console half is a filter-and-order over the existing lane list, and "not listed means `Uncategorized`, never hidden" is exactly what the renderer already does for an off-lane value. The describe says so.
- **Ordered list over a flag.** A `hideEmptyLanes` flag would make lanes depend on data, remove the drop target the user wants (the empty lane to move a card into), and cannot order. The list answers both halves of the card (hide the always-empty lane, choose the order) with one stable key. Right.
- **Grammar at the spec, membership at the gate.** The spec refuses what it can see without the object (shape, emptiness); lint refuses what needs the object (membership, duplicates) at `os validate`, `os build` and the publish door, so a misspelled lane never reaches a board. The split keeps the published JSON Schema exact and is the same division `groupByField` already uses. Right.
- **Not a record filter.** The docblock and describe refuse the reading that `lanes` hides records; the view's `filter` is named as the way to keep records off the board. This matches the measured HotCRM case (the view already filters out completed tasks; only the empty lane was the defect).
- **No default, nothing retroactive.** Existing boards carry no `lanes` and parse and draw as before.
- **Strictness holds.** The block stays a `strictObject`; an undeclared key is still refused (control in the spec test).

Should-fix (none blocks the contract):
- **S1** The `.describe()` does not say the key is declared ahead of its reader; the changeset and docblock do. A blanket liveness row cannot carry `authorWarn`, so an author of `lanes` today gets no "nothing draws it yet" word from `os validate`. Either a one-clause note in the describe or a drilled `kanban.lanes` row graded `planned` with `authorWarn` (the #28191 `seriesBy` shape) would close that; can ride the console card, which flips it to live anyway.
- **S2** `checkKanbanLanes` reads inline `options[].value` only. A field with `options` whose option is hidden by `visibleWhen` is still a valid lane (its stored value exists), which is right; but an `optionsExtensions`/`picklistExtensions`-style widening of inline options, if one ever lands on `FieldSchema`, would need to join this map. A note on the module docblock is enough; no code change owed now.

**VERDICT: PASS**
